{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"Every Tuesday, a paper crane appeared on the windowsill of the town library. Each was folded from a different page: a recipe, a bus timetable, once a map of the moon.

Mara, the librarian, began lining them up behind the circulation desk. By winter, the cranes formed a small, uneven flock.

“Throw them away,” said the caretaker. “They’re only scraps.”

But Mara liked the thought of someone leaving a little work behind for a stranger. She set out a sign: IF THESE ARE YOURS, THANK YOU.

The following Tuesday, there was no crane. Instead, she found a square of blank yellow paper.

Mara turned it over. Nothing. After closing, she tried folding it herself. Her first crane had a crooked neck and one wing smaller than the other. She left it on the windowsill.

The next morning, a man was standing outside, smiling at it. He came in carrying a stack of yellow squares.

“My wife used to make them,” he said. “She died in the spring. I found her box of paper, and I didn’t know what else to do with it.”

Mara glanced at her clumsy crane. “I’m sorry. I think I used too many creases.”

“She would have liked it,” he said. “She was always trying to teach someone.”

They sat at a table while he showed her how to fold the wings. A student waiting for a computer asked to join them. Then the caretaker pulled up a chair.

When they locked the doors that evening, three new cranes stood on the windowsill, facing the street."}
